How does it compare to Ubuntu? I thought of going back to it but heard some complains about Ubuntu being like the Microsoft of Linux (if that even makes sense)

Mint is Ubuntu (and Debian). This is an oversimplification: Mint puts a highly functional installer, drivers, software, and other important things on top of a solid Linux substrate. Then just when you thought it was all about functionality they make versions with different desktop environments to suit everything from very old to very new machines. And patching and system updates are simple and just work.

I have a 9 year old Dell laptop running Mint Cinnamon (high-end graphics version). It's pretty and everything works, even the the funky trackpad and backlit keyboard. And it is still fast and can use the latest 4.4 kernel.

The computer I just bought is the latest 6th gen Intel I7 with on-board sky lake graphics. So new most drivers don't work well with the graphics. So I switched to the MATE desktop (an older, more stable and less bling vesion). It works, too, and also works with the latest 4.4 kernel.

This a very wide range of possible hardware. That Mint just works is a testament to the developers and the community. I have it installed on other desktops and laptops, but this range shows the breadth.
